findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now an uninstantiable abstract class
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` was changed from a concrete `DetectorHandler` (with a stub `evaluate` returning `[]`) to `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass`. `StatefulDetectorHandler` declares four abstract members (`counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`) none of which are implemented here. Because `MetricAlertFire` is auto-registered in the grouptype registry with `detector_handler = MetricAlertDetectorHandler`, any `Detector` row with `type == "metric_alert_fire"` will cause `Detector.detector_handler` (`group_type.detector_handler(self)`) to raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class`, which propagates out of `process_detectors` and aborts processing of the whole batch. The previous stub at least ran safely; either keep a concrete stub implementation of the abstract methods or drop the `detector_handler` assignment until the real implementation lands.

findings.title: Expected occurrences built with wrong group_key/value; assertions don't verify occurrence contents
findings.body: In `TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe` the expected occurrence is built via `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, ...)` but `evaluate_group_key_value` is invoked with group key `"group_key"` and value `10`, so the handler's real `build_occurrence_and_event_data` produces a fingerprint `["<id>:group_key"]` that differs from the expected `["<id>:val1"]`. Similarly `test_state_results_multi_group` builds the `group_2` expectation with value `6` while the packet carries `10`. These assertions can only pass because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` hardcodes `id="eb4b0acffadb4d098d48cb14165ab578"` and `IssueOccurrence` equality is effectively id-based, meaning every mock occurrence compares equal to every other. As a result the new tests do not actually verify that the hook is called with the correct group key, value, priority or fingerprint, and `assert_has_calls(..., any_order=True)` in the multi-group test would pass even if the same occurrence were produced twice. Either pass the matching arguments and assert on the handler's call arguments (e.g. via `mock.patch.object(MockDetectorStateHandler, 'build_occurrence_and_event_data')`), or give each mock occurrence a distinct id derived from the group key.

findings.title: evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` was changed to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still reads "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`". Implementers reading the docstring will get the wrong contract; update it to describe the dict keyed by group key.
